text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The nationalist Fatherland and Freedom party held a congress Saturday and decide to merge with fellow nationalist grouping LNNK. A June 21 congress will formalise the merger.
- A group of Russian MPs, led by the head of the parliamentary group for cooperation with the Baltic states, will visit Latvia May 5-9.
- The Euromoney financial magazine published ratings of the Baltic states, which showed Latvia advancing to 63 from 75, with Estonia at 69 and Lithuania at 72.
- The corpse of a Swedish professor, missing since March, was found by fishermen in a lake near the port town of Liepaja.
- Industrial output rose 5.3 percent n March.
- Two teenagers caused a train to derail on the Riga-Mazheikiai line by removing a rail.
- President Guntis Ulmanis told foreign ambassadors on Sunday that Latvia should double spending on cooperation with NATO.
- The newspaper publishes a TV address by Ulmanis on the 7th anniversary of Latvia's declaration of independence from the former Soviet Union.
- On the 5th anniversary of the Latvian language law, the head of the state language centre said that many Russian-speakers still do not speak Latvian.
- Revised land tax bills shocked many landowners as they rose to 100 lats and more.
- The finance ministry's long-term forecasts show GDP growth of between 4 and 5 percent from 1998. Latvia will meet the Maastricht conditions by 2002, the forecast said.
- Shares in Riga Shipyard will be quoted from today.
